intent: The small muted caption naming a SidebarGroup.
typical_uses: The caption at the top of a sidebar section

dont_use_when.situation: A caption for a form control outside the sidebar

invariants.text: Collapsed to the icon rail the label fades out and pulls its own 32px row away with a negative top margin, so the rows below move up; it is not removed from the DOM.
SidebarGroupLabel renders a plain div with no role and no link to the group.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's useRender takes an element or a function of the label's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how the caption becomes a heading or a `label` element.

good.title: A caption that labels the section's search field

bad.title: A caption expected to name the section for assistive tech
bad.why: The label is a plain div and the group a plain div with no role, so nothing names the section; render the label as a heading, or give the group `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's useRender takes an element or a function of the label's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how the caption becomes a heading or a `label` element.
